items.title: Iranian missile partially collapses Haifa building, injuring at least 10

featured_image.name: Israel Says Haifa Residential Building Suffers Direct Hit in Iran Attack

items.description: An Iranian ballistic missile slammed into a residential building in the northern Israeli city of Haifa on Sunday, partially collapsing the structure and injuring at least four people as rescue teams scrambled to search for others potentially trapped beneath the rubble. The strike marks one of the most damaging single hits on Israeli civilian infrastructure since the war between the U.S.-Israel coalition and Iran entered its sixth week.

items.title: Iran launches Wave 96 strikes on Israel and Gulf energy sites

featured_image.name: Israel targets Iranian missile crews as Haifa's historic mosque damaged in  strike

items.description:
Iran launched a sweeping barrage of missiles and drones targeting Israel and energy infrastructure across the Persian Gulf on Sunday, marking the 37th day of the war that began when the United States and Israel struck Iran on February 28. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said the attacks, designated Wave 96 of Operation True Promise 4, were retaliation for U.S.-Israeli strikes on a bridge in Karaj and petrochemical facilities in Mahshahr.[1][2][3][4]

An Iranian ballistic missile scored a direct hit on a seven-story residential building in the northern Israeli city of Haifa, injuring four people, the Israeli military and Magen David Adom emergency service confirmed to AFP. Among the wounded was an 82-year-old man in serious condition who was pulled from the rubble after being struck by heavy debris. Images published by medics showed smoke rising from the flattened remains of the building in a densely populated area.[5][6][7]

Separately, an Iranian missile struck the Neot Hovav industrial complex near Beersheba in southern Israel, according to Israeli army radio. The site, one of Israel's largest chemical manufacturing zones, has been hit repeatedly during the conflict, with previous strikes in late March triggering fires and hazardous material concerns.[8][9][10]

items.title: Iran surpasses 500 ballistic missiles fired at Israel in five-week war

featured_image.name: Iran's use of cluster munitions against Israel may be a war crime

items.description: More than 500 ballistic missiles have been launched from Iran at Israel since the start of the war on February 28, the Times of Israel reported Sunday, as the conflict entered its 37th day with no ceasefire in sight. Roughly half of those missiles have carried cluster munition warheads, according to the Israel Defense Forces, a tactic that has exposed vulnerabilities in Israel's layered air defense systems and killed at least four civilians in documented strikes.[1][2][3]

items.title: Polymer prices surge over 40% as Iran war chokes global supply

featured_image.name: Iran could disrupt the Strait of Hormuz with drones for months | Reuters

items.description:
Five weeks into the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is rippling far beyond oil markets, triggering a crisis in global plastics and petrochemicals that is pushing up prices for everyday goods from bottled water to food packaging.

Polymer prices have surged roughly 41 to 42 percent since hostilities erupted on February 28, according to industry tracker Polymer Update, with some segments such as PVC in India climbing as much as 78 percent. The disruption has proven stubbornly persistent: even as crude oil corrected from its peak above $126 per barrel, polymer prices have continued to climb as physical supply shortages deepen across Asia and Europe.[1][2]

items.title: Iran launches missiles at Israel, Kuwait after rejecting Trump ultimatum
items.description: Iran launched missiles and drones at Israel and Kuwait early Sunday, hours after its military command rejected President Donald Trump's ultimatum to reach a peace deal within 48 hours or face devastating strikes on its vital infrastructure. Both Kuwait and Israel said their air defense systems were activated to respond to the latest barrage, extending a conflict now in its sixth week.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Putin's approval hits lowest point since Ukraine invasion

featured_image.name: Russia is restricting access to Telegram, one of its most popular ...

items.description:
Vladimir Putin's approval rating has fallen to its lowest point since the eve of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, as public anger mounts over the Kremlin's decision to restrict and ultimately block Telegram, the country's most widely used messaging platform.

Data from Russia's Public Opinion Foundation (FOM), published in early April by The Moscow Times, shows trust in Putin fell five percentage points in a single week — from 76% to 71% — in a survey conducted between March 27 and 29. It marks the sharpest weekly decline the pollster has recorded since at least 2019. Figures from the state-run Russian Public Opinion Research Center (VTsIOM) corroborate the trend, showing Putin's approval at 70.1% while disapproval rose from 14.8% in January to 18.3% in March.[1][2]
